fullPassage: It is important to remember that a misunderstanding never ended by an argument but by a sympathetic desire to see the other person's view. As Buddha said, "Hatred never ended by hatred but by love." Here is an example: Pat Duffy was selling cars for General Motors. If a buyer made a negative remark about the car he was selling, Pat would get upset at the customer. He would talk back to the customer and win lots of arguments, but he didn't sell many cars. Finally, he learned to handle the customers and here is how. If a customer said, "This GM car is no good! I would rather buy a Ford car," Pat, instead of arguing, said, "Ford cars are good, and it is a fine company." This made the customer speechless. There was no room for argument. Now instead of wasting time arguing about Ford cars, Pat got off that subject and concentrated on the GM cars he was selling.
